caption: James Mooney, the Smithsonian ethnologist listed among the Native American Church's 1918 incorporators, photographed circa 1900.
alt: Black-and-white studio portrait of a mustached man in a dark suit and bow tie.
credit: Bureau of American Ethnology, Bulletin 99, plate I (1901) / Smithsonian Libraries via Internet Archive Book Images
note: Not the document itself: no facsimile of the filed Articles of Incorporation could be located online (only transcriptions). Mooney, the Smithsonian anthropologist who defended peyote religion before Congress, is named among the incorporators/signers listed in the draft's people field, so his portrait stands in as the best available fallback (category 3, portrait).
